metadata.title: README Checker: Does the README Actually Work?
metadata.bookend_exempt_reason: Opens on my own intro, then the hesitant writer; no terms card (cut 4 keeps the how out of the executive summary); no verdict card or Your Turn (cut for the 2-4 minute limit). The locked ClaudeTitleOutro is replaced by an own drawn outro (B14) because it hard-codes @NikBearBrown, and the assignment forbids the instructor's credit line.
metadata.audience: hiring managers and engineers reviewing a Software Engineer candidate
metadata.source_doc: PROJECT-BRIEF.md; APPENDIX.md; two manual README runs on 2026-10-13 (github.com/LavanyaRajesh24/webapp, github.com/heroku/node-js-getting-started); prior work in SOURCES.md (ExecutionAgent, Installamatic, Runme, Doc Detective)

beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Luh-vun-ya. My final project is the README Checker. Nothing is built yet.

shot.visual_intent: Title picture: the README Checker name, 'final project pitch · Lavanya', and 'nothing is built yet', beside a README page and an open box.
shot.motion_claim: Title picture: the README Checker name, 'final project pitch · Lavanya', and 'nothing is built yet', beside a README page and an open box.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture per beat on a cream stage; the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: The question isn't how to fix a broken README. It's how to find out if it works.

show.event: types 'How do I fix a broken README'
corrects 'fix' to 'find' as the voice says it

props.text: How do I fix a broken README

beats.motion_claim: The writer types the naive question (fix) and corrects it to the real one (find).

qc.sparse_reason: Hesitant-writer bookend: the correction is the motion.

beats.narration_text: A new engineer opens a README and follows the setup steps. A step fails, and they can't tell if the problem is them, or the instructions.

shot.visual_intent: A README page (grey lines); a cursor walks down and an X lands. Key line: 'Is it me, or the instructions?'
shot.motion_claim: A README page (grey lines); a cursor walks down and an X lands. Key line: 'Is it me, or the instructions?'

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture per beat on a cream stage; the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: The README Checker will follow a project's setup instructions exactly as written, and tell you which step is broken, and why. It only reports. It won't fix anything.

shot.visual_intent: A README page on the left, an arrow, and a report on the right whose rows get a check, a warning and an X. Key line: 'Which step is broken, and why.' Small 'reports only · won't fix'.
shot.motion_claim: A README page on the left, an arrow, and a report on the right whose rows get a check, a warning and an X. Key line: 'Which step is broken, and why.' Small 'reports only · won't fix'.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture per beat on a cream stage; the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: On October thirteenth, I followed my own web app's README in a fresh copy. The clone link was a placeholder, a config file was missing, and the health check returned five oh three.

shot.visual_intent: My webapp README as a grey-line page with seven rows; a mark lands beside each: placeholder warning, pass, fail, skipped, placeholder warning, fail, fail.
shot.motion_claim: My webapp README as a grey-line page with seven rows; a mark lands beside each: placeholder warning, pass, fail, skipped, placeholder warning, fail, fail.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture per beat on a cream stage; the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: I wrote that README, and I couldn't see what was wrong with it. Every engineer who joins a project pays for that, in lost time.

shot.visual_intent: A terminal panel with my real output from 2026-10-13: the migrate error and the 503 response. Key line: 'The writer can't see it. The next engineer pays for it.'
shot.motion_claim: A terminal panel with my real output from 2026-10-13: the migrate error and the 503 response. Key line: 'The writer can't see it. The next engineer pays for it.'

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture per beat on a cream stage; the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: What exists already? Doing it by hand. Heroku's starter app worked for me, but its README asked for a tool I didn't need, and skipped the npm version it wanted. By hand, you only find what you happen to hit.

shot.visual_intent: A terminal panel with my real Heroku output: the npm engine warning and 200 OK.
shot.motion_claim: A terminal panel with my real Heroku output: the npm engine warning and 200 OK.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture per beat on a cream stage; the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: Second, CI. My project's CI installs Node and the database with its own steps, separate from the README. It tests the code, not the instructions a person reads.

shot.visual_intent: My CI panel on one side, the README page on the other; the CI checks pass, the README is never touched.
shot.motion_claim: My CI panel on one side, the README page on the other; the CI checks pass, the README is never touched.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture per beat on a cream stage; the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: Doc tools. Runme runs a README's code blocks, but you judge the output. Doc Detective checks docs against the product, using tests you write first.

shot.visual_intent: Two labelled cards: Runme (runs a README's code blocks · you judge the output) and Doc Detective (tests docs against the product · you write the tests first).
shot.motion_claim: Two labelled cards: Runme (runs a README's code blocks · you judge the output) and Doc Detective (tests docs against the product · you write the tests first).

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture per beat on a cream stage; the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: And research. ExecutionAgent, published in 2025, set up and tested thirty three of fifty open source projects. Installamatic installed twenty one of forty Python projects. Both aim to get a project running, not to say which README line is wrong.

shot.visual_intent: Two result cards with their published numbers: ExecutionAgent 33 / 50, Installamatic 21 / 40, each labelled with its venue. Key line: 'Built to get it running, not to judge the README.'
shot.motion_claim: Two result cards with their published numbers: ExecutionAgent 33 / 50, Installamatic 21 / 40, each labelled with its venue. Key line: 'Built to get it running, not to judge the README.'

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture per beat on a cream stage; the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: So CI skips the README, doc tools leave the judging to you, and AI agents work around it. The README Checker will run it as written, and say which line broke. That's why it's worth building.

shot.visual_intent: A comparison table: by hand, CI, Runme, Doc Detective, AI setup agents, README Checker (planned) × 'runs the README itself' and 'says which line broke, on any README'. Rows land as named.
shot.motion_claim: A comparison table: by hand, CI, Runme, Doc Detective, AI setup agents, README Checker (planned) × 'runs the README itself' and 'says which line broke, on any README'. Rows land as named.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture per beat on a cream stage; the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: Now the method. A command line tool, in a public GitHub repo, that will run every README step inside a throwaway container, deleted after each run.

shot.visual_intent: Open box (the container); the README drops in. Key line: 'Runs every README step in a throwaway container.'
shot.motion_claim: Open box (the container); the README drops in. Key line: 'Runs every README step in a throwaway container.'

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture per beat on a cream stage; the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: It will run one step, read the real output, and decide: continue, stop, or mark it unclear. The AI picks the move, but every result comes from a command that ran.

shot.visual_intent: Run → read → decide loop; a dot travels the loop.
shot.motion_claim: Run → read → decide loop; a dot travels the loop.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture per beat on a cream stage; the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: Then it will write a report: pass, warning, or fail for each step, with the README line and the real error. This one is a mock up. It isn't built yet.

shot.visual_intent: A readable report mock-up for my webapp README with README line numbers, stamped 'constructed mock-up'.
shot.motion_claim: A readable report mock-up for my webapp README with README line numbers, stamped 'constructed mock-up'.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture per beat on a cream stage; the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: The data: about ten small sample projects I'll make myself. Half get one planted problem, like a missing file. Half work. So I know the right answer before the tool runs.

shot.visual_intent: Ten sample boxes; five get a terracotta dot (a planted problem); an answer-key page appears beside them.
shot.motion_claim: Ten sample boxes; five get a terracotta dot (a planted problem); an answer-key page appears beside them.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture per beat on a cream stage; the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: Step by step. One: run one sample README in a container, and write report dot md with real exit codes. Two: add the agent loop, and a prompt contract my code checks. Three: build the samples and the answer key. Four: run the evaluation.

shot.visual_intent: Four numbered rows landing in order, the first marked 'first milestone'.
shot.motion_claim: Four numbered rows landing in order, the first marked 'first milestone'.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture per beat on a cream stage; the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: Do I have what I need? Docker is on my laptop, the code goes on my GitHub, and the model calls go through Claude Code on my university login, which I've already used for a course agent. It's about one call per step, so my laptop is enough.

shot.visual_intent: A four-row checklist: Docker, GitHub account, Claude access, compute; a check lands on each as it is named.
shot.motion_claim: A four-row checklist: Docker, GitHub account, Claude access, compute; a check lands on each as it is named.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture per beat on a cream stage; the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: The risk: a README can contain any command. So the container gets no secrets, and no access to my files. Vague steps get marked unclear, not guessed.

shot.visual_intent: A locked box swapped for a fresh one; a vague step marked 'unclear'.
shot.motion_claim: A locked box swapped for a fresh one; a vague step marked 'unclear'.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture per beat on a cream stage; the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: How will I know it worked? I'll run it on all ten samples, and compare each report to my answer key. Two numbers: planted problems caught at the right line, and false alarms on the projects that work.

shot.visual_intent: Answer key and the tool's report side by side with a comparison mark; two empty score slots: caught ? / 5 and false alarms ? / 5. Small 'these numbers don't exist yet'.
shot.motion_claim: Answer key and the tool's report side by side with a comparison mark; two empty score slots: caught ? / 5 and false alarms ? / 5. Small 'these numbers don't exist yet'.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture per beat on a cream stage; the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: It worked if it catches at least four of the five planted problems at the right line, with at most one false alarm, and every verdict comes from a command that ran. Three or fewer, or two false alarms, and it didn't. Either way, I'll write up where Claude was wrong.

shot.visual_intent: Two columns: 'It worked if' (≥ 4 / 5 caught at the right line · ≤ 1 false alarm · every verdict backed by a real exit code) and 'It didn't if' (≤ 3 / 5 · ≥ 2 false alarms).
shot.motion_claim: Two columns: 'It worked if' (≥ 4 / 5 caught at the right line · ≤ 1 false alarm · every verdict backed by a real exit code) and 'It didn't if' (≤ 3 / 5 · ≥ 2 false alarms).
